followUp.title: Both halves of the fence compare the path as written, so a read through a symlink alias is never judged; the root node_modules holds 25 such aliases into tracked source
followUp.where: genesis/orchestrator/read-fence-preload.c:50-73 (normalize), :75-95 (absolute), :172 (strstr "/node_modules" exemption); genesis/orchestrator/read-fence.mjs:254 (path.resolve, no realpath), :266 (node_modules regex)
followUp.evidence:
The hole is real and I reproduced it end to end, but it is latent at this HEAD: no named test reads through an alias today, so no stale green exists yet.

**Code trace (HEAD 9c203f961)**
- `genesis/orchestrator/read-fence-preload.c:50-73` (`normalize`) and `:75-95` (`absolute`) are purely lexical. `:172` then drops any in-root path containing `/node_modules`.
- `genesis/orchestrator/read-fence.mjs:254` uses `path.resolve` with no realpath, and `:266` returns null for any path with a `node_modules` segment.
- `genesis/orchestrator/gate-input-audit.mjs:40` (`SUITE_IMPLICIT_READS`) keys only `.npmrc`, `package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml` and `pnpm-workspace.yaml`. Nothing keys the tracked source a workspace link points at, so the comment at `:36-38` ("what shapes node_modules") is false for workspace links.

**Real repo**
- `/projects/elohim/node_modules` holds 25 links that resolve into tracked source, for example `@elohim/epr -> elohim/sdk/epr-ts`, `elohim-orchestrator -> genesis/orchestrator`, `@elohim/a2o -> genesis/a2o`.
- With the shim built by `buildPreload`'s own flags, `cat /projects/elohim/elohim/sdk/epr-ts/package.json` logs one row; `cat /projects/elohim/node_modules/@elohim/epr/package.json` (same bytes, tracked) logs none.

**End-to-end reproduction** (scratch repo `/tmp/claude-0/e11-review/verify-shim-c-1/root`, using copies of the real `suite-run.mjs`, `read-fence.mjs`, `read-fence-preload.c`, with `node_modules/pkg -> ../lib` and every test declared `reads: []`):

| Test | How it reads `lib/` | `suite-run.mjs named` |
|---|---|---|
| hole-fs | `fs.readFileSync(ROOT/node_modules/pkg/secret.txt)` | pass, no READ-FENCE line, exit 0 |
| hole-child | `cat node_modules/pkg/secret.txt` with cwd ROOT | pass, no READ-FENCE line, exit 0 |
| hole-proc | `fs.readFileSync('/proc/self/cwd/lib/secret.txt')` | pass, no READ-FENCE line, exit 0 |
| control-fs | `fs.readFileSync(ROOT/lib/secret.txt)` | "undeclared read: lib/secret.txt", exit 1 |
| control-child | `cat lib/secret.txt` | "undeclared read: lib/secret.txt (open, coreutils)", exit 1 |
| import-bare | `import { secret } from 'pkg'` | "undeclared read: lib/index.mjs (module)", exit 1 |

**What narrows it (my refutation attempts)**
- Module loads are not affected. Node realpaths the resolved module, so a bare import of a workspace package is judged by both halves (the import-bare row). The same holds for fenced node children and `.bin` wrappers.
- The live route is therefore only a literal alias path handed to an fs API or to a non-node child, or `/proc/self/cwd`.
- I scanned all 60 named test files plus the 120 files they transitively import, and the declared shell scripts, for `node_modules/<workspace>`, `/proc/self/cwd|root` and `preserve-symlinks`. No hits. The one `node_modules` path, `genesis/scripts/ci/runner-authority-ci.mjs:117`, executes the untracked `.bin/tsx`.
- The shim's `strstr` at `:172` does not swallow any tracked path: the only two tracked names containing "node_modules" have `_node_modules`, not `/node_modules`.
- I did not run the full real suite under the fence to confirm this dynamically; the "no alias read today" conclusion rests on the static scan.

**Why it does not block landing**
The orchestrator key covers every read the named side makes today on this dimension, so landing as-is is neither unsound nor red on either device. The exposure starts when a future edit to a named test or a declared module adds an alias read: that run would be recorded green with the read unkeyed, and later changes to the aliased source would reuse it.
followUp.fix:
Judge the resolved path as well as the written one, and apply the node_modules exemption to each separately. This can follow the landing.

1. **`genesis/orchestrator/read-fence.mjs`**
   - In `install()`, before the `wrap` loop at `:283`, capture the unwrapped resolver: `const realNative = fs.realpathSync.native`.
   - In `rel` at `:254`, after `s = path.resolve(s)`, compute `real = realNative(s)`. On ENOENT, resolve the deepest existing ancestor and re-append the remainder.
   - In `read()` at `:269-275`, classify both `s` and `real` when they differ, and report if either is judged. The regex at `:266` then exempts a path only when the path being classified is itself inside `node_modules`, so `<root>/node_modules/.pnpm/...` stays exempt and `<root>/elohim/sdk/epr-ts/...` reached through a link is judged.
   - Judging both also keeps a tracked symlink's own path declared (for example `elohim/sdk/schemas/current`) alongside its target.

2. **`genesis/orchestrator/read-fence-preload.c`**
   - Split the classification body of `seen()` (`:166-174`) into a helper that takes an absolute path.
   - In the content wrappers (`open`/`open64`/`openat`/`openat64` from `:186`, plus `fopen` and the exec path), after the real call returns `fd >= 0`, `SYS_readlink` `/proc/self/fd/<fd>` and pass the result to the helper when it differs from the lexical path. This costs one readlink per successful open and closes `node_modules` links, `/proc/self/cwd` and any other symlink for content reads.
   - For path-only calls (`stat`/`access`/`readlink`/`opendir`), call `realpath(3)` under the existing `busy` guard only when the lexical path was dropped by the `/node_modules` test at `:172` or lies outside root.
   - The `strstr` exemption at `:172` then applies per classified path, as in the node half.

3. **`genesis/orchestrator/read-fence.test.mjs`**: add the three cases from the reproduction (fs through a node_modules link, a `cat` child through the link, `/proc/self/cwd`), each expected to be a violation.

4. **`genesis/orchestrator/gate-input-audit.mjs:36-38`**: correct the comment. Workspace links are tracked source, not install state.

followUp.title: A child can drop the fence, or have its rows discarded, without any row reaching the check
followUp.where: genesis/orchestrator/read-fence-preload.c:32-47 and :159-161/:329-331 (lazy init, no constructor), :338-339 (`followed` ignores GATE_READ_FENCE_FILE), :349-362 (exec table), :151-152 (log open failure returns silently); genesis/orchestrator/read-fence.mjs:163 (rows with no file are dropped), :130-134 (a preload-carrying child is never judged on the node side); genesis/orchestrator/suite-run.mjs:41-42 (log lives in a 0700 mkdtemp)
followUp.evidence:
I could not refute it: routes (a), (b) and (c) reproduce end to end against the real fence at 9c203f961, and (d) reproduces at the shim level. No named test at HEAD takes any of the four routes, so the hole is latent and landing as-is does not make dev unsound or red today.

Setup: shim built from HEAD's read-fence-preload.c with the recipe's flags (`cc -O2 -shared -fPIC -march=x86-64 … -ldl`), a byte-identical copy of read-fence.mjs in a scratch repo, run on shem (uid 0, full uid_map), judged with `node read-fence.mjs check`. Everything is under /tmp/claude-0/e11-review/verify-shim-c-2/ (run.sh, probe.c, fr/, out/); the review checkout is unchanged (status clean).

Control: a plain `cat <root>/secret/g.txt` child gives the row and "undeclared read", check exit 1. So the harness does catch what it should.

| Route | What the child did | Read succeeded | Log | check exit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| a1 | libc-only program: `clearenv()` then `execv` of cat | yes | no file | 0 |
| b1 | `execle(cat, …, empty env)` | yes | no file | 0 |
| b2 | `fexecve` with empty env | yes | no file | 0 |
| c1 | `env -u GATE_READ_FENCE_FILE cat <repo file>` | yes | `{"file":"","kind":"child","op":"open","path":"secret/d.txt"}` | 0 |
| d | cat as uid 65534, log in a root-owned 0700 dir | yes, exit 0 | no file | not run |

Code path for each:
- **(a)** read-fence-preload.c:32-47 reads the environment lazily; with it cleared, :39 sets ready=0 and judge_exec returns at :331.
- **(b)** The exec table at :349-362 has no execl/execle/execlp/fexecve/execveat.
- **(c)** `followed` at :338-339 checks only LD_PRELOAD, LOG and ROOT; read-fence.mjs:163 then drops the row with no file.
- **(d)** emit() at :151-152 returns silently when the log cannot be opened; suite-run.mjs:41-42 puts the log in a 0700 mkdtemp. With the same child and uid but a writable log, the row lands.
- **Node half** read-fence.mjs:129-134 returns null for any preload-carrying child, so it does not help in any of the four.

Corrections that narrow the reviewer's claim:
1. **execl alone is not an escape.** With the environment inherited (b3), the child's own shim logs the read and the check exits 1. Only a replaced environment (execle, fexecve, execveat) escapes.
2. **`env -i cat <repo file>` is caught on shem** (a2, a3: "child cleared the read fence", exit 1). /usr/bin/env here is the coreutils-single multi-call binary, which evidently initialises the shim before env clears. A standalone libc-only env would have the shape of a1; whether ethosengine has one was not checked.
3. **(d) loses nothing at HEAD.**
   - runner-capture-activation.test.mjs:387-395 and :482-490 do spawn node as uid 65534 on shem.
   - The real file passes under the fence, 41/41, with the log in a closed 0700 dir.
   - A root-run analog of that exact child, which can write the log, emits zero rows.
   - The reviewer's "appendFileSync throws" needs the child to report a violation first, and this child reports none.
   - Caveat: /tmp/claude-0 is itself 0700, so my uid-65534 runs could not load the scratch shim through an absolute path. I used a relative LD_PRELOAD from an inherited cwd for the shim-level run.
4. **No present trigger.** Among the non-tree entries of suite-reads.json, only runner-capture-activation uses `uid:`. `env -i` appears only in app/elohim-app/scripts/hc-mesh.sh:2184, which no named entry declares. clearenv, execle and fexecve appear nowhere outside the fence's own files.

Why it does not block: each route needs a future named-test change (clear the environment before the first libc call, replace the environment through a non-interposed exec, drop only GATE_READ_FENCE_FILE, or drop uid and read the repo). The fence already carries declared residuals of the same class (fixture-bound unseen children; raw syscalls can never be interposed). The fix is small, though, and every file it touches is a gate governance path, so folding it into this landing saves one fenced landing per device.

Side observation, outside this finding: this review worktree has no node_modules, so gate-evidence.test.mjs under the fence logs 334 "read of another checkout" rows for /projects/elohim/node_modules/.pnpm/…. That may be an artifact of this un-installed checkout and of the OTHERS list I built by hand.
followUp.fix:
Four small changes. The first three were validated in a scratch copy (verify-shim-c-2/patched.c → shim-patched.so): a1, b1, b2 and c1 all flip to "child cleared the read fence", check exit 1. Control and b3 are unchanged, and the three real named tests I ran (runner-capture-activation, gate-evidence, gate-task) show no new reasoned rows — row counts match unpatched for the first two, and gate-task was run patched only (0 rows).

1. **read-fence-preload.c, after :107** — snapshot the fence at load, which closes (a):
   `__attribute__((constructor)) static void fence_loaded(void) { init(); refresh_file(); }`

2. **read-fence-preload.c:338-339** — extend `followed`, which closes (c) at the exec:
   `&& (!file[0] || env_has(envp, "GATE_READ_FENCE_FILE", file))`
   The `!file[0]` guard keeps the runner, which has no file, able to start test processes.

3. **read-fence-preload.c, after :362** — interpose the missing exec entry points, which closes (b):
   - `execl` and `execle` collect the varargs and call the shim's own `execve`; `execlp` calls the shim's `execvp`.
   - `fexecve` resolves the program from `/proc/self/fd/<fd>`, calls `judge_exec`, then the real function.
   - `execveat` resolves through `absolute(dirfd, path, …)`, calls `judge_exec`, then the real function.

4. **suite-run.mjs:41-42 and read-fence-preload.c:152** — let a uid-dropped child write its rows, which closes (d). Not validated end to end; I only showed that the row lands when the log is writable.
   - After `mkdtempSync`: `writeFileSync(log, ''); chmodSync(log, 0o666); chmodSync(scratch, 0o711);`
   - In `emit()`, when the log open fails, write one line to fd 2 and `_exit(126)` instead of returning, so a lost row fails closed.

Optional: at read-fence.mjs:163, treat an in-repo `child` row with an empty file as a violation. The real runs I made produced no such rows, but the comment there says the runner can emit them, so this needs a full-suite run first.

What no preload fix closes, and should be named as a residual: raw `syscall(SYS_execve / SYS_openat2)`, and a child with a hand-built environment that is fixture-bound by design.

followUp.title: Reads made inside glibc or by direct syscall never reach the shim: scandir, glob, nftw, fts, realpath, openat2
followUp.where: genesis/orchestrator/read-fence-preload.c:188-238 (the interposed set)
followUp.evidence:
The hole is real and reproduced end to end on shem (AlmaLinux 10.2, glibc 2.39), but no named test at 9c203f961 reads the repository through it, so dev's `orchestrator` key is not unsound today.

**Traced path**
- `genesis/orchestrator/read-fence-preload.c:188-238` interposes only the public `open*`, `fopen*`, `*stat*`, `access*`, `readlink*`, `opendir` and `chdir`.
- glibc's `scandir`, `scandirat`, `ftw`/`nftw`, `fts_*`, `glob`, `realpath` and `canonicalize_file_name` reach the kernel through hidden internal aliases, so `seen()` (line 158) never runs for them. A raw `syscall(SYS_openat2)` or `syscall(SYS_openat)` bypasses it trivially.
- `read-fence.mjs:130-134` (`judgeSpawn`) returns null for any child that carries the preload, so the shim is the only witness for a non-node child.
- `judgeRows` (`read-fence.mjs:160-169`) can only judge rows the shim wrote.

**Reproduction 1: shim alone**
Shim built with the exact flags from `read-fence.mjs:185` (`cc -O2 -shared -fPIC -march=x86-64 … -ldl`), probe at `/tmp/claude-0/e11-review/verify-shim-c-3/p.c`, run against a fake root.

| Call | Shim rows | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `opendir`, `stat`, `open`, `fdopendir` (controls) | 1 each | seen |
| `scandir`, `scandirat` | 0 | listed 5 entries |
| `nftw`, `ftw` | 0 | visited 5 |
| `fts` | 0 | 7 entries |
| `glob` | 0 | 3 matches |
| `realpath`, `canonicalize_file_name` | 0 | resolved the symlink |
| raw `openat2`, raw `openat` | 0 | printed the file content |

**Reproduction 2: through the real `suite-run.mjs named`**
Fixture repo at `/tmp/claude-0/e11-review/verify-shim-c-3/fr` holding unmodified copies of `read-fence.mjs`, `read-fence-preload.c`, `suite-run.mjs` and `gate-input-audit.mjs` with its imports.
- `hole.test.mjs` declares `reads: []` and spawns the probe with cwd at the repo root. It ran `scandir und`, `nftw und`, `fts und`, `glob und/*` and `openat2 und/f.txt`, and got the content `secret-undeclared`. The test passed, there were no READ-FENCE lines, and `suite-run named` exited 0.
- Control: the same test file layout using `opendir und` and `open und/f.txt` produced "undeclared listing: und" and "undeclared read: und/f.txt", and `suite-run named` exited 1.

**Why it does not block landing**
I ran the whole named side (60 files: 42 + 17 + 1) with the fence environment `runSide` sets, plus an audit-only preload chained after the shim (`/tmp/claude-0/e11-review/verify-shim-c-3/audit.c`). It logs every call to `scandir`/`scandir64`/`scandirat`, `glob`/`glob64`, `ftw`/`nftw` and their 64 variants, `fts_open`, `realpath`, `__realpath_chk` and `canonicalize_file_name`.
- 46,140 calls logged. Non-node calls whose path resolves inside the checkout or the main checkout: 0.
- Non-node callers were `clippy-driver`, `cargo`, `rustup` and `rustc` (from `cargo-lint.test.mjs`), `python3.12` (`__realpath_chk`, from `prepush-self.test.mjs`) and `coreutils` (`canonicalize_file_name`). Every one of their paths was under the test's TMPDIR fixture or `/opt/rust`.
- Node made 41,576 `scandir64` and 100 `realpath` calls (libuv). Those processes are witnessed by the JS half (`read-fence.mjs:283-290`), not the shim.
- Children with in-repo shim rows in that run were node, git, bash, coreutils and epr. epr imports `glob` and `realpath` but made no call to either.
- Mainstream tools are seen under the shim: `realpath`, `readlink -f`, bash globbing and `pwd -P`, python `glob` and `os.path.realpath`, `tar`, `rg`.

**Limits of this check**
- Raw-syscall reads cannot be audited here (no strace). The only raw-syscall-heavy programs spawned are node (JS fence) and the Rust toolchain on fixtures.
- 11 tests failed in the first group in my run; the review worktree has no `node_modules`. I did not analyse them and they are outside this finding.
- The named suite itself runs `cargo clippy` on a temp fixture via `cargo-lint.test.mjs`, so my run invoked cargo indirectly. All its output went to scratch TMPDIR, and `git status --porcelain --ignored` on the worktree was identical before and after.

**Corrections to the reviewer's text**
- Node imports `scandir64`, not `scandir`.
- GNU make calls `glob` with its own directory callbacks, which use the public `opendir`, so it is probably seen.
- The comment at `read-fence-preload.c:1-4` ("sees what every dynamically linked child … opens, stats, lists or executes") is an overclaim, and the branch names this residual nowhere: a grep of the diff for scandir, nftw, fts, openat2, io_uring, landlock and syscall finds nothing.
followUp.fix:
Can follow the landing; nothing at HEAD exploits it.

1. **`genesis/orchestrator/read-fence-preload.c`, after line 238:** add forwarders in the existing `REAL` + `seen()` style.
   - `scandir`, `scandir64` → `seen(AT_FDCWD, p, "opendir")`; `scandirat`, `scandirat64` → `seen(d, p, "opendir")`.
   - `ftw`, `ftw64`, `nftw`, `nftw64` → `seen(AT_FDCWD, root, "opendir")`; `fts_open`, `fts64_open` → the same for each `argv[i]`.
   - `glob`, `glob64` → `seen(AT_FDCWD, <literal directory prefix of the pattern, up to the last '/' before the first of * ? [ {>, "opendir")`.
   - `realpath`, `__realpath_chk`, `canonicalize_file_name` → `seen(AT_FDCWD, p, "stat")`.

   Logging only the root or literal prefix as a listing is sound under `judgeRead` (`read-fence.mjs:85-89`): either a declared prefix covers the whole subtree, or the row is an "undeclared listing".

2. **`genesis/orchestrator/read-fence.test.mjs:171` (the "REAL preload" test):** compile a small C probe with the same `cc` and assert that `scandir`, `nftw`, `fts`, `glob` and `realpath` on an undeclared path each produce a violation.

3. **`read-fence-preload.c:1-7` and the RESIDUAL paragraph at `read-fence.mjs:17-24`:** replace "sees what every dynamically linked child … opens, stats, lists or executes" with the true bound. A dynamically linked program that issues syscalls directly (raw `openat`/`openat2`, io_uring, a cgo-linked Go binary) is loaded but unseen, and `judge_exec` (`read-fence-preload.c:328-346`) cannot tell. LD_PRELOAD cannot close that class; only a kernel-level backstop such as Landlock could, and I did not test one here.

followUp.title: emit() can write past its stack buffer and drop the row; every intercepted call needs about 33 KB of stack; execve(NULL) crashes
followUp.where: genesis/orchestrator/read-fence-preload.c:133-150 (line[3*PATH_MAX], `sizeof line - at` after at has passed the end), :126 (6-byte escape per control byte), :144, :164-167, :51, :80 (PATH_MAX buffers per frame), :271 (strchr on a NULL name)
followUp.evidence:
All three parts reproduce at 9c203f961, but none is reachable from the suite as it stands, so this can follow the landing.

I built `/projects/elohim/.worktrees/review-nt-e11/genesis/orchestrator/read-fence-preload.c` with the gate's own flags (`cc -O2 -shared -fPIC -march=x86-64 ... -ldl`, from `read-fence.mjs:185`) on shem (AlmaLinux 10.2, gcc 14.3.1) and ran a toy probe under it. Scratch files are in `/tmp/claude-0/e11-review/verify-shim-c-4/`.

**1. `emit()` overflow and dropped row (`:133-150`) — confirmed.**
- `json_string` (`:123`) stops at `at + 7 < cap`, so `at` can reach about cap-6.
- The fixed `,"exe":` append at `:147` adds snprintf's untruncated return value (7), pushing `at` past `sizeof line` (12288).
- At `:149`, `sizeof line - at` underflows and snprintf writes `}\n\0` up to 4 bytes past `line[]`; `:150` then returns without writing the row.
- Measured with a path of N 0x01 bytes under the fence root:

| N control bytes | Plain build | `-D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=3` build |
|---|---|---|
| 2030 | 1 row, 12284 bytes | 1 row |
| 2036 | 0 rows, exit 0 (silent) | not run |
| 2040 and above | 0 rows, exit 0 (silent) | `*** buffer overflow detected ***`, exit 134 |

- The gate build has no fortify and no stack protector by default on this gcc, so the real behaviour is a silent drop plus a small out-of-bounds stack write.
- Reach: it needs about 2036 control bytes in one path (6 output bytes each), or a path and `/proc/self/exe` both near PATH_MAX and full of quotes or backslashes. Of the 21702 tracked paths at HEAD, none contains a control byte, quote or backslash, and the longest is 208 bytes.

**2. Stack use — confirmed; the reviewer's thresholds are slightly off.**
- Frame sizes from objdump of the gate build: `seen.part.0` 0x2018, `absolute` 0x1048 (plus `normalize`'s `out[PATH_MAX]`), `emit` 0x4028, `judge_exec` 0x20f8. That is about 16.5 KB for any intercepted call, about 24.6 KB when a row is emitted, and about 33 KB only on the exec path.

|---|---|---|
| 16 KB | exit 139 | exit 139 |
| 20 KB | ok | not run |
| 24 KB, 28 KB | ok | exit 139 |
| 32 KB and above | ok | ok, 1 row |

- ark's declaration contract refuses this key outright: `loader keys would run code the passport never hashed` (elohim/ark/core/src/declaration.rs:306). A library built per device by the device's cc is exactly that.
- The verdict is not keyed on the observation. It is keyed on a hand-kept list, and the observation only vetoes. Variables read are not observed at all.

What the branch does prove is valuable: 60 of 88 files have nameable reads, and a list at the commit can be the key.

**Is LD_PRELOAD the primitive to generalise?** No.
- It is blind to static programs, and `just`, which starts every recipe, is static on this device. It is also blind to raw syscalls.
- It is cooperative: a child that clears its environment escapes. The branch detects that and banishes the file to the tree side, which is how 15 of 28 tree files got there.
- It puts a per-device C build on the gate's path, the hazard class of row 29.

**Simplest sound primitive: absence.** Run the recipe in a checkout that contains only the declared reads at the commit.
- The verdict is then a function of the keyed bytes by construction, not by detection.
- Static, set-id and env-clearing children are covered.
- The named residuals close: gitignored manifest copies, listings that depend on other names, and working tree against commit.
- It is what ark's Task already models: `input` is a TreeView the carrier materialises (elohim/ark/core/src/task.rs:4, :289). A sibling or CI carrier must do it anyway.

I tried it on this device (shem). A `git archive` of the declared union at HEAD is 634 of 21,701 files, 11 MB, built in 1.3 s. The 60 named files then ran there with `env -i`, no fence and no shim: 1,125 of 1,136 tests pass in 144 s. Of the 11 failures, the five in runner-capture-activation are my scratch directory's 0700 parent (EACCES for uid 65534) and four are submodule manifests I did not materialise; I did not open the output of the other two.

Caveats for absence:
- node_modules must be replicated so workspace links resolve inside the view, not symlinked whole.
- A hard-coded absolute path can still reach the real checkout. Landlock closes that natively in ark's supervisor: ABI 4 is available here, as are mount and user namespaces and fanotify; ethosengine is unprobed.
- For cargo gates, use a persistent sparse worktree at a stable path, or a Landlock allow-list over the real checkout. A fresh archive resets mtimes and would rebuild everything.
- Absence gives soundness but can let an optional read pass vacuously. An observer is still useful as a cross-check and to generate the list, outside the trust path. That is row 28's `the scan becomes a cross-check`.

**What survives a move to absence:**
- suite-reads.json as the view definition, and suite-run.mjs as the runner (the fence environment replaced by materialising the view)
- the gate / gate-tree split
- SUITE_READ_LISTS and suiteReadSet key composition
- suite-list.test.mjs, the notInSuite discovery, and the test hygiene edits
- the pool-policy enrolment

What leaves the gate path is read-fence-preload.c, most of read-fence.mjs and read-fence.test.mjs: about 920 of 1,923 lines, and the C toolchain dependency. They can stay as an offline tracer.

**Is 53 s worth it?** Not as seconds.
- The saving lands on about 40% of commits and not on the lane's own habit commit (finding 1), so roughly 20 s expected per commit.
- Recorded landings run from 70 s to 162 min, dominated by cargo gates and by three unkeyed JS gates the habit ledger lists at 460 s.
- The tree half's 94 s is paid on every landing; the author attributes 86 s of it to two files. serving-receipt (49 s) is a fixture move. gate-input-audit (37 s) is not inherently tree: it reads every `.rs` and manifest, so an extension walk keys it, and preflight's checkReadSets (gate-preflight.mjs:257) already runs the same audit. Fixing those two is worth more than this branch's expected saving on every landing, in tens of lines.
